FA No. 13 of 2020
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the 
appellant.
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for 
respondent No. 1.
In pursuance to the notices issued by 
the coordinate Bench of this Court on 
24.02.2020 to respondent Nos. 2 and 3, the 
steps were taken by the appellant on 
28.02.2020. There is an office report which 
shows that the address of respondent No. 2, as 
given in the Memo of Appeal is not the 
correct address and it has been found that 
respondent No. 2 is residing at Mussoorie.
As far as respondent No. 3 is 
concerned, there is a report that respondent 
No. 3 has left the given address.
In view of the office report dated 
07.07.2020, the learned counsel for the 
appellant is directed to take fresh steps for 
effecting service upon respondent Nos. 2 and 
3 on the correct address within the period of 
10 days from today.
List the matter after the service upon 
respondent Nos. 2 and 3 is complete.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)

FA No.13 of 2020
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate, for the 
appellant.
Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan, Advocate, 
for the respondent.
Mr. Pankaj Kumar, Advocate, holding 
brief of Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate, for the 
respondent. 
This is a defendant’s first appeal 
preferred against the impugned judgment and 
decree dated 13.08.2019, as rendered in Suit 
No.151 of 2013, seeking the decree of partition 
and permanent injunction.
The appeal was preferred by the 
appellant along with the delay condonation 
application CLMA No.1571 of 2020, seeking 
condonation of 49 days of delay, on the ground 
that there was a delayed information, which has 
imparted to the appellant by his counsel, who 
was conducting the case before the learned trial 
court.
The delay condonation application 
preferred by the defendant, the delay is being 
opposed by the respondent nos.1, 2 and 3, by 
filing objection through IA No.7255 of 2020.
Simultaneously, the respondents, who 
has filed the objection against the delay 
condonation application has also preferred a  cross appeal under Order 41 Rule 22 of the 
CPC, through IA No.7259 of 2022.
After having heard the learned counsels 
for the parties, and particularly, considering the 
reasons for delay, which cannot be directly
attributed to the appellant causing delay in 
filing the delayed appeal, due to the fault of the 
counsel, who had given a delayed information. 
The delay of 49 days, which has chanced in 
filing the appeal, would stand condoned.
Accordingly CLMA No.1571 of 2020, would 
stands disposed of.
As a consequence of the order of 
allowing the delay condonation application, the 
objection filed to the delay condonation 
application by respondent no.1, through IA 
No.7255 of 2022, would too stand disposed of.
List this first appeal, as well as the cross 
appeal under Order 41 Rule 22 of CPC, for 
hearing at an admission stage next week. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 22.08.2022
NR/

02.09.2022 FA No.13 of 2020
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Present proposed First Appeal has 
been filed against the judgment and 
decree dated 13.08.2019, passed by the 
Civil Judge (Senior Division), Dehadun in 
Original Suit No.151 of 2013, 
“Prabhatesh Pratap Singh vs. Prabhan 
Pratap Singh and Others”, whereby, the
Original Suit, filed for partition, 
mandatory and prohibitory perpetual 
injunction, has been allowed and a 
preliminary decree has been passed. 
Heard Mr. Piyush Pant, the learned 
counsel for the appellant-defendant and 
Mr. Yashpal Singh, learned counsel for 
the respondent no.1-plaintiff. 
None is present on behalf of the 
respondent nos.2 & 3.
Cross-objection has also been filed 
by the respondent no.1-plaintiff. 
Admit the appeal.
Summon the lower court records.
List this case on 24.11.2022. 
In the facts and circumstances of 
the case, the effect and operation of the 
impugned judgment and decree dated 
13.08.2019 is stayed till the next date of 
listing. 
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) 02.09.2022
 JKJ/Pant
